observation.visible_scene: A close, oblique view of a long white board whose surface carries a continuous serpentine (zigzag) groove. A single glossy red ball rests in that groove. The background is a plain off-white wall; a pale wooden surface is partly visible at the lower-right edge, and a static 'AMAKANDU' watermark sits in the upper-left corner.
visible_changes: The red ball rolls along the serpentine groove, repeatedly rising over the wave crests and dropping into the troughs (its vertical position in the frame oscillates while it advances).

Relative to the board, the ball travels left-to-right: it begins on the left side of the diagonal seam line on the board and ends on the right side of that seam, confirming genuine object motion rather than only camera motion.

The camera itself pans/tracks along the board: the seam line and the wave pattern steadily shift toward the left edge of the frame, and the patch of wood at the lower-right grows larger, so part of the apparent ball movement is camera movement.
A bright specular highlight on the ball shifts position as the ball moves and rotates; this is a reflection on the ball's surface, not a separate object.
The ball's motion is already underway at the first frame and is still continuing at the last frame; no start or stop is shown inside the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the ball entered the groove before t=0 and where the groove leads after t=1.33 s.
Whether the ball eventually stops, exits the track, or continues oscillating beyond the crop.
The full length and end conditions of the board/track.
uncertain_details: Whether the camera motion is handheld or mounted, and the exact relative speeds of camera pan vs. ball roll.
Whether the ball's forward speed is constant or varying; only the oscillatory path is clearly visible.
The material identities of the ball and board (only appearance is supported).
